name: Shammah
overview: Shammah was a male warrior known as the third of "the thirty," an elite group of David's mighty men. He is identified as the son of Agee, though his tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture. His role as one of David's renowned fighters highlights his importance in the military exploits recorded during David's reign.
namesAndTitles: The name Shammah means "astonishment" in Hebrew. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaning that may reflect the impact or character of this individual as remembered in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Shammah was the son of Agee. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections or relatives are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shammah's significance lies in his position as a prominent warrior within David's elite fighting force known as "the thirty." His mention in 2 Samuel 23:11 underscores the valor and loyalty of David's men, who played a crucial role in securing and maintaining David's kingdom. As the son of Agee, Shammah's legacy is preserved through his distinguished military service, reflecting the strength and faithfulness valued in God's anointed king's supporters.
